data.note:
Reflection: Unblinded mitomycin C (PubChem CID 5746, CHEMBL105 DNA inhibitor) matches BBBC021 annotation DNA damage, so my revised conclusion DNA damage (p=0.46) is correct. Phenotypic logic was sound despite budget-exhausted PI follow-up: nuclear enlargement with increased DNA content, smooth mononucleate morphology, no multinucleation proxy increase, and intact tubulin correctly favored G2-arrest DNA damage over Aurora failed-cytokinesis polyploidy, though atlas was split (NSC 2/4 DNA damage vs kNN 6/10 Aurora).

PubChem/ChEMBL confirms DNA inhibitor mechanism. Literature supports: mitomycin C forms interstrand crosslinks and double-strand breaks [PMID 17512921, 41199376, 35349830] and DNA-repair deficiency causes G2 arrest with nuclear size changes [PMID 10834928], consistent with enlarged nuclei/G2 phenotype measured. Next step in real lab would be gamma-H2AX + cell-cycle flow as proposed.

reflection.text:
Unblinding: mitomycin C, PubChem CID 5746 / ChEMBL CHEMBL105, annotated DNA inhibitor. Verdict correct: DNA damage, but review request for experiment was justified and my first p=0.61 was over-calibrated.

What the evidence got right:
- Low-intermediate doses consistently showed single enlarged nuclei phenotype: e3 (0.3uM) nuc_area z=+23.6, e7 (1uM) nuc_area z=+26.4 frac_large_nucleus z=+9.5, e8 (0.1uM) nuc_area z=+20.5. This matches DNA damage G2 arrest with increased DNA content and large-nucleus fraction, not actin/tubulin disruption. Lookups e24/e25 (name and BBBC021 structure agree on DNA inhibitor) and literature search e26/e27 are consistent with mitomycin C as DNA crosslinker / DSB inducer PMID 17512921, PMID 35349830, PMID 41199376, and with DNA damage-induced stalled replication / G2 arrest PMID 23319047, PMID 10834928.
- Microscopist at active dose e6 (density lower vs DMSO, 6 observations, candidates: Aurora, DNA damage, DNA replication) correctly kept both polyploidy hypotheses alive and ruled out microtubule/actin classes, which I then correctly down-weighted in hypothesis updates e14/e22 (Protein synthesis 0.02-0.04, Microtubule destabilizer/stabilizer 0.01).
- Second conclusion p=0.46 better reflected uncertainty after review.

What misled me and why:
- Acquisition choice: I spent all 4 wells on single replicates across extremes: e2 10uM rep1, e3 0.3uM, e7 1uM, e8 0.1uM from list_available_experiments (8 doses 0.003-10uM, 4/4 wells left). Including the divergent cytotoxic well e2 (155 cells, tub_glcm_contrast z=+25.1, act_glcm_contrast z=+14.5, tub_std z=+14.2) diluted every dose-response. As a result nuc_area rho=-0.20 p=0.8 e10, nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.20 p=0.8 e13, and even informative trends frac_large_nucleus rho=+0.80 p=0.2 e15, frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.80 p=0.2 e16, frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=+0.80 p=0.2 e20 were non-significant with n=4. I cannot claim dose-dependence from those p-values.
- Atlas comparison was split and shared-phenotype confounded: e4 NSC 1/2 DNA damage, kNN 9/10 Aurora; e9 NSC 2/4 DNA damage, kNN 6/10 Aurora. The review correctly noted 6/10 neighbors and higher mean similarity favored Aurora, while enlarged nuclei, increased integrated DNA, large-nucleus fraction up, mitotic fraction down, no microtubule/actin disruption is predicted by both Aurora failed cytokinesis and DNA damage G2 arrest. I weighted NSC vote and nuclear enlargement toward DNA damage e14 (0.62 vs 0.28) without a direct multinucleation measure.
- Phenotype description did not resolve it: e5 (high dose, 0 observations) uninformative; e19 (dose_code 3, 0.1uM, 4 fields, density similar vs DMSO, 7 observations, candidates: unknown) was the requested mono- vs multi-nucleated polyploid / pH3-like scoring, but summary gave no clear multinucleate count. Dose-response of nuc_solidity rho=-0.80 p=0.2 e21 and cell_count rho=-0.40 p=0.6 e17 were also underpowered. Without replicates I could not test the discriminating prediction (Aurora = multinucleate polyploidy vs DNA damage = single enlarged nuclei).

What I missed / would do differently:
- Strategy: should not acquire 10uM as first probe for DNA damage; should have allocated 2-3 replicates at 0.1-0.3uM (the onset window seen in e8/e3) plus 0.03uM threshold control, instead of one-offs at 1uM and 10uM. That would have given power for frac_multinucleate_proxy and nuc_solidity, and avoided cytotoxic tubulin/actin texture e11 rho=+0.80, e12 rho=+1.00 that mimics cytoskeletal effects.
- Calibration: with single-replicate, n=4, p~0.2 trends and NSC 2/4 split, p=0.61 was too high; p=0.46 was still a weak lead, appropriate to request experiment as reviewer did.

Next lab step I proposed remains appropriate given unblinding: gamma-H2AX foci IF, PI cell-cycle for G2 accumulation, p53/p21 Western vs reference DNA-damage and Aurora controls, EdU/pH3 to quantify S vs M, with replicated dose-response at 0.1-1uM - no clinical claim implied.
what_was_right: Consistent nuclear enlargement at 0.1-1uM e3 e7 e8 identified DNA damage polyploidy/G2 phenotype; e25/e24 DNA inhibitor annotation matches mitomycin C crosslink/DSB mechanism PMID 17512921 PMID 35349830 PMID 41199376 PMID 10834928 PMID 23319047
what_was_wrong: High dose e2 cytotoxic texture misled cytoskeletal readouts e11 e12; kNN 9/10 then 6/10 Aurora in e4 e9 with shared enlarged-nuclei/low-mitotic phenotype inflated runner-up; dose-responses e10 e13 e15 e16 e20 underpowered p>=0.2 due to n=4 and inclusion of e2

## Reflection

Unblinding: mitomycin C, PubChem CID 5746 / ChEMBL CHEMBL105, annotated DNA inhibitor. Verdict correct: DNA damage, but review request for experiment was justified and my first p=0.61 was over-calibrated.

What the evidence got right:
- Low-intermediate doses consistently showed single enlarged nuclei phenotype: e3 (0.3uM) nuc_area z=+23.6, e7 (1uM) nuc_area z=+26.4 frac_large_nucleus z=+9.5, e8 (0.1uM) nuc_area z=+20.5. This matches DNA damage G2 arrest with increased DNA content and large-nucleus fraction, not actin/tubulin disruption. Lookups e24/e25 (name and BBBC021 structure agree on DNA inhibitor) and literature search e26/e27 are consistent with mitomycin C as DNA crosslinker / DSB inducer PMID 17512921, PMID 35349830, PMID 41199376, and with DNA damage-induced stalled replication / G2 arrest PMID 23319047, PMID 10834928.
- Microscopist at active dose e6 (density lower vs DMSO, 6 observations, candidates: Aurora, DNA damage, DNA replication) correctly kept both polyploidy hypotheses alive and ruled out microtubule/actin classes, which I then correctly down-weighted in hypothesis updates e14/e22 (Protein synthesis 0.02-0.04, Microtubule destabilizer/stabilizer 0.01).
- Second conclusion p=0.46 better reflected uncertainty after review.

What misled me and why:
- Acquisition choice: I spent all 4 wells on single replicates across extremes: e2 10uM rep1, e3 0.3uM, e7 1uM, e8 0.1uM from list_available_experiments (8 doses 0.003-10uM, 4/4 wells left). Including the divergent cytotoxic well e2 (155 cells, tub_glcm_contrast z=+25.1, act_glcm_contrast z=+14.5, tub_std z=+14.2) diluted every dose-response. As a result nuc_area rho=-0.20 p=0.8 e10, nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.20 p=0.8 e13, and even informative trends frac_large_nucleus rho=+0.80 p=0.2 e15, frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.80 p=0.2 e16, frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=+0.80 p=0.2 e20 were non-significant with n=4. I cannot claim dose-dependence from those p-values.
- Atlas comparison was split and shared-phenotype confounded: e4 NSC 1/2 DNA damage, kNN 9/10 Aurora; e9 NSC 2/4 DNA damage, kNN 6/10 Aurora. The review correctly noted 6/10 neighbors and higher mean similarity favored Aurora, while enlarged nuclei, increased integrated DNA, large-nucleus fraction up, mitotic fraction down, no microtubule/actin disruption is predicted by both Aurora failed cytokinesis and DNA damage G2 arrest. I weighted NSC vote and nuclear enlargement toward DNA damage e14 (0.62 vs 0.28) without a direct multinucleation measure.
- Phenotype description did not resolve it: e5 (high dose, 0 observations) uninformative; e19 (dose_code 3, 0.1uM, 4 fields, density similar vs DMSO, 7 observations, candidates: unknown) was the requested mono- vs multi-nucleated polyploid / pH3-like scoring, but summary gave no clear multinucleate count. Dose-response of nuc_solidity rho=-0.80 p=0.2 e21 and cell_count rho=-0.40 p=0.6 e17 were also underpowered. Without replicates I could not test the discriminating prediction (Aurora = multinucleate polyploidy vs DNA damage = single enlarged nuclei).

What I missed / would do differently:
- Strategy: should not acquire 10uM as first probe for DNA damage; should have allocated 2-3 replicates at 0.1-0.3uM (the onset window seen in e8/e3) plus 0.03uM threshold control, instead of one-offs at 1uM and 10uM. That would have given power for frac_multinucleate_proxy and nuc_solidity, and avoided cytotoxic tubulin/actin texture e11 rho=+0.80, e12 rho=+1.00 that mimics cytoskeletal effects.
- Calibration: with single-replicate, n=4, p~0.2 trends and NSC 2/4 split, p=0.61 was too high; p=0.46 was still a weak lead, appropriate to request experiment as reviewer did.

Next lab step I proposed remains appropriate given unblinding: gamma-H2AX foci IF, PI cell-cycle for G2 accumulation, p53/p21 Western vs reference DNA-damage and Aurora controls, EdU/pH3 to quantify S vs M, with replicated dose-response at 0.1-1uM - no clinical claim implied.

What was right:
- Consistent nuclear enlargement at 0.1-1uM e3 e7 e8 identified DNA damage polyploidy/G2 phenotype; e25/e24 DNA inhibitor annotation matches mitomycin C crosslink/DSB mechanism PMID 17512921 PMID 35349830 PMID 41199376 PMID 10834928 PMID 23319047

What was wrong or missed:
- High dose e2 cytotoxic texture misled cytoskeletal readouts e11 e12; kNN 9/10 then 6/10 Aurora in e4 e9 with shared enlarged-nuclei/low-mitotic phenotype inflated runner-up; dose-responses e10 e13 e15 e16 e20 underpowered p>=0.2 due to n=4 and inclusion of e2

Proposed next experiment: Re-acquire dose_code 3 (0.1uM) in triplicate plus 0.03uM onset vs DMSO, blinded scoring of mono- vs multinucleate large nuclei and pH3 mitotic index; follow with gamma-H2AX IF and PI flow for G2 vs failed cytokinesis vs Aurora control
